sections.html:
Every tax office sits in Cadiz, the county seat. The clerk's real estate line is (270) 522-6661, and the office at 38 Main Street opens weekdays from 8:00 am until 4:00 pm.

  • Sheriff, (270) 522-6014: collects the current year's bills.
  • Property Valuation Administrator (PVA), (270) 522-3271: assigns values, takes exemption applications and holds the meeting that has to precede any appeal.
  • County clerk, (270) 522-6661: handles recording, marriage licenses and delinquent taxes. Vehicle titles and renewals use (270) 522-0217.
  • County attorney, (270) 522-4733: mails the notices that precede a delinquent tax sale.

The clerk's office closes for part of the Trigg County Ham Festival each October, so plan payoff requests around festival week.

sections.h2: Lakes, second homes and the local market
sections.html:
Water shapes everything here. Trigg covers 481 square miles, 40 of them water, on the far southwest edge of Kentucky beside Lake Barkley. Land Between the Lakes National Recreation Area reaches into the county, and Lake Barkley State Resort Park and Prizer Point Marina pull visitors to the shore. Cadiz is known as the Antique Capital of Western Kentucky. Lyon, Caldwell, Christian, Calloway and Marshall counties border it, along with Stewart County, Tennessee.

Population was 14,061 in 2020 and is estimated at 14,512 for July 2025. The county has 7,733 housing units but 6,060 households, and 23.4 percent of units were vacant in 2020. Rentals stood empty at a rate of 11.7 percent. A county built around two large lakes can show that pattern, and it means a seller may compete with seasonal and vacant homes.

Seniors make up 24.9 percent of residents, and the 2020 median age was 46.8. No building permits were reported for 2025. With that many older owners, the homestead exemption is worth asking about early. The average trip to work takes 24.3 minutes.

The regular due date under state law falls at year end. Early payers by November 1 get a 2 percent discount; the printed amount applies through year end; January payments carry 5 percent; anything later carries 10 percent. If the state delays bills, the Department of Revenue can swap in an alternative schedule: two full months to pay after mailing, discount in month one, printed amount in month two, a 5 percent penalty for a month and 10 percent after.

Bills unpaid when the sheriff's period closes on April 15 go to the clerk as certificates of delinquency.

The clerk runs one delinquent tax sale a year, at the end of July in the year after the taxes were due. The order of events is the same each year.

  • The list of certificates is published in the Cadiz Record in early June.
  • Buyers register by close of business in early July.
  • The sale takes place at the clerk's office, 38 Main Street, at 9:00 am in late July.

The list is open for viewing at the clerk's office on weekdays and on the clerk's website. Owners can pay at the clerk any time before the sale; money that arrives afterward is returned. Some advertised bills are excluded under KRS 134.504(10)(b). Each year's dates appear on the clerk's delinquent tax page.

sections.h2: If your bill is past due
sections.html:
Pay before April 15 if you can. After that date the file moves from the sheriff to the clerk, and the county attorney starts mailing notices. The second notice names the sale date, and the list is published in the newspaper ahead of it.

You can still pay at the clerk's office up to the day of the sale. An owner who is selling should settle early, because a bill bought by an investor has to be paid to that investor, usually at a higher cost. Ask the clerk whether any older year is open on your parcel, so none of them turns up at closing.

The PVA's conference comes first, before or during the inspection period, and the roll stays open to view for two weeks in May. An owner who has been through the conference files with the county clerk on the next workday after that window.

The local board then convenes within roughly five weeks and can sit for up to five days. The board expects paper, such as lot and building details, insurance policies, what the house cost to build or comparable listings, and rejects an appeal without it. Separately, the PVA appraises most homes from nearby sales and walks each parcel at least every fourth year. Personal property that is taxable must be listed with the PVA between New Year's Day and May 15, and a later filing is treated as omitted.

A resident owner who is 65, or totally disabled, can deduct $49,100 from the assessment for 2025 and 2026, provided the house is owned, lived in and kept up on January 1. Applications go to the Trigg County PVA before December 31. Someone classified as totally disabled by an agency outside Kentucky renews every year. Owners with a service-connected total disability and people found totally and permanently disabled by Social Security file once.

Request the current payoff from the sheriff and ask the clerk if a certificate of delinquency exists. Under KRS 134.015 the January 1 owner carries that year's tax as a personal debt, and a delinquency lien can outlast a transfer by up to eleven years. When an investor bought the certificate at the July sale, the payoff goes to that investor.

Gather the figures before you list. Call the sheriff at (270) 522-6014 for the current bill, then the clerk at (270) 522-6661 about any older certificate. Give the written amounts to the closing agent so they come out of your proceeds. A cash buyer can take a lake-area house as it stands, with no staging or repairs, and the tax balance is paid at closing. Compare what you would keep after payoffs rather than the headline offer.

Bring a photo ID and the parcel number to each office, and ask for a written figure with the date it was calculated. Penalties and interest change the amount, so a figure from close to the closing date is the one a title agent will use. If you inherited the house, bring the paperwork showing who has authority to sell it.

Keep copies of every receipt you collect along the way.

faqs.q: Who collects current property tax in Trigg County?
faqs.a: The sheriff, at (270) 522-6014. After the April 15 cutoff the county clerk, (270) 522-6661, takes over unpaid bills.

faqs.q: When does the Trigg County clerk hold its delinquent tax sale?
faqs.a: Once a year, near the end of July. Each year's dates are posted on the clerk's delinquent tax page.

faqs.q: Can I still pay after my Trigg County bill is advertised?
faqs.a: Yes, up to the sale. The clerk's office at 38 Main Street accepts delinquent payments before that date and returns any that arrive afterward.

faqs.q: What is the Trigg County homestead exemption worth?
faqs.a: $49,100 in assessed value for 2025 and 2026. Seniors and totally disabled owners can file with the PVA at (270) 522-3271 before the year ends.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Trigg County house that owes back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Closing clears the lien out of your sale money, so collect written payoffs from the sheriff and the clerk beforehand.
